raw_graphql_pull_request.body: [Feat] mem_cache: Elastic hybrid-SWA KV pools (kvcached VMM), with an Intel XPU path ## Motivation This PR ports sgl-project/sglang#13581 onto current main and adds an Intel XPU backend. With `SGLANG_ENABLE_ELASTIC_MEM_POOL=1`, the full-attention and sliding-window (SWA) KV pools of a hybrid-SWA model no longer have fixed sizes. Each pool reserves a large virtual range and backs only its current size with physical pages. The two pools trade pages at runtime: when one pool runs hot and the other runs cold, the cold pool's tail is drained and unmapped, and the freed memory is mapped into the hot pool. Total device memory stays the same; only the split between the pools changes. On gpt-oss-20b on an Intel Arc Pro B60, elastic memory raised throughput by 18-24% and cut mean TTFT by 13-22% across three workloads, using the same device memory. ## Dependencies - **[sgl-project/sglang#13581](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/13581)** (open), "Integration with elasticmem": the design this PR builds on. The first commit re-implements it on current main. If #13581 merges first, this PR rebases onto it and keeps only the XPU commit and the fixes listed under "Changes from #13581". - **[ovg-project/kvcached#501](https://github.com/ovg-project/kvcached/pull/501)** (open), "Intel XPU (Level Zero) backend for kvcached VMM": required for the XPU path. `ElasticXPUMHATokenToKVPool` calls `kvcached.vmm_ops`, which needs kvcached built from that PR with `KVCACHED_BACKEND=xpu`. The CUDA path keeps #13581's `kvcached.etensor` requirement and does not depend on #501. ## Modifications | Commit | Scope | |---|---| | Port elasticmem (kvcached VMM) hybrid-SWA pools onto main | The orchestrator, allocators and CUDA pool; configurator and scheduler wiring; startup validation; post-capture KV sizing turned off under elastic memory; CPU unit tests | | elasticmem: add an XPU path backed by kvcached Level Zero | `ElasticXPUMHATokenToKVPool`, its XPU startup checks, the XPU docs and `scripts/emem/dev_xpu.sh` | ### How it works - **`ElasticMempoolOrchestrator`** (`mem_cache/elastic/elasticmem_orchestrator.py`) picks the hottest and coldest pool by token usage. It resizes when all three hold: - the usage gap is at least `SGLANG_ELASTIC_MEM_RESIZE_TRIGGER_DIFF_RATIO` (0.2); - the hot pool is above `SGLANG_ELASTIC_MEM_MAP_THRESHOLD` (0.9); - the cold pool is below `SGLANG_ELASTIC_MEM_UNMAP_THRESHOLD` (0.8). - **`ElasticTokenToKVPoolAllocator`** (`mem_cache/elastic/elastic_allocator.py`) marks the cold pool's tail as a shrink candidate and withholds its free slots. - The shrink happens once every in-use tail slot can be evicted from the radix tree. Until then it waits, or it is cancelled if the pools even out. - The withheld slots still count as available, so admission is unchanged. - **`ElasticSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator`** owns the orchestrator and both sub-allocators. After each resize it re-syncs the `SWAKVPool` sizes and the full-to-SWA index mapping. - **Pools:** `ElasticMHATokenToKVPool` on CUDA (kvcached `ETensor`), and `ElasticXPUMHATokenToKVPool` on XPU (kvcached `vmm_ops`, see below). - **Scheduler:** `maybe_init_elastic_mem` attaches the allocator to the tree cache, and `try_resize` runs after each scheduled batch. - **`UnifiedTreeCore.component_evictable_device_indices`** reports which slots can be evicted, so a tail is shrunk only when it can be drained. ### Changes from #13581 - **Device sync before unmap:** unmap is not ordered with the stream. With overlap scheduling, the forward still in flight can read slots that were just freed or evicted. The allocator therefore synchronizes the device before it unmaps. The cost is one wait per shrink. - **Shrink floors:** each pool stops shrinking at a floor that keeps a max-length request schedulable. This keeps the scheduler's startup capacities and request-length limits valid: - the full pool keeps at least `max_req_len`; - the SWA pool keeps at least the sliding window plus one prefill chunk, or `max_req_len` when chunked prefill is off; - neither floor goes above the pool's startup size. - **Leftover pages:** pages too few for the hot pool to use go back to the cold pool instead of staying unmapped. - **Cheaper drain checks:** while a shrink is pending, the full-tree walk behind `component_evictable_device_indices` runs again only after the number of in-use tail slots or the evictable total changes. - **Shutdown handling:** kvcached shuts down at exit, and before a terminating signal whose handler is still the default. Signals that are ignored or have a Python handler are left alone, so an ignored signal no longer shuts kvcached down while the process keeps running. - **Tree core default:** main defaults `SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND` to rust, and only the Python core has `component_evictable_device_indices`. When the variable is unset, elastic memory picks python, as `--enable-kv-cache-sharding` does. An explicit non-python choice is refused. - **Startup validation** refuses: - devices other than CUDA and XPU; - `--page-size > 1`, unified memory, the page-major layout, the memory saver and speculative decoding; - PD disaggregation and `--enable-hierarchical-cache` (both register KV buffers by row count once, and a resize changes the row count); - mxfp8/fp4 KV, `SGLANG_USE_HND_KVCACHE`, and pure-SWA models. - **Env vars** are renamed to `SGLANG_ENABLE_ELASTIC_MEM_POOL` and `SGLANG_ELASTIC_MEM_*`. ### XPU pool - **kvcached backend:** uses `kvcached.vmm_ops` with kvcached's Level Zero backend (ovg-project/kvcached#501): - `init_kvcached` runs once per process; - `create_kv_tensors` creates one allocator group per pool; - `map_to_kv_tensors` / `unmap_from_kv_tensors` work by page offset. One offset covers that page of K and of V in every layer. - **No zero page:** Level Zero has no shared zero page, so every row the pool exposes is mapped before first use. After each resize, the K/V views and `_kv_buffer_descs` are re-sliced to exactly `size + page_size` rows. The data pointers stay the same. - **Virtual range:** sized from total device memory. Physical memory only moves between the two pools. - **Page size 1:** `intel_xpu` serves `--page-size 1` through sgl-kernel-xpu's gather fallback (sgl-kernel-xpu#454), which is slower than its paged kernel. `--attention-backend triton` works where that build is missing, or where its non-paged path rejects attention sinks (gpt-oss). - **XPU startup checks:** kvcached must be installed, and kvcached's own SGLang autopatch (`ENABLE_KVCACHED` / `KVCACHED_AUTOPATCH`) must be off. ## Accuracy Tests gsm8k (`sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`, all 1,319 questions) on two servers side by side, each on its own B60 with the flags below. Each server ran gsm8k, then 128 × 8192/1024 requests, then gsm8k again. The elastic server resized once during the middle step (full 52,505 → 77,823 tokens, SWA 52,505 → 28,671). | Server | Before | After | Change | |---|---|---|---| | elastic | 0.544 | 0.542 | -0.2 | | static | 0.510 | 0.528 | +1.8 | The static server, which never resizes, moved 1.8 points between two runs, so the -0.2 is within run-to-run noise. Five fixed prompts at temperature 0 (64 new tokens) gave identical text: - static vs elastic; - elastic before vs after its resize; - elastic before any resize vs after the 2-hour soak below. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Measured on the current head of this branch. In these runs the shrink floors don't bind: the full pool only grew, and the SWA floor (128 + 4096 tokens at the B60 default chunk size) is far below the 20,479-token minimum the SWA pool reached. The device sync before unmap is included in the resize times below. **Setup:** | | | |---|---| | Hardware | Intel Arc Pro B60 (24 GB), one card per server | | Driver | compute runtime 26.18.38308.1, Level Zero loader 1.26.2 | | Software | SGLang main `51d5502aff` + this PR, torch 2.14.0+xpu, kvcached with the XPU backend, sgl-kernel 0.11.0 | | Model | openai/gpt-oss-20b | | Flags | `--device xpu --attention-backend triton --page-size 1 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 1.0 --context-length 65536` | | A/B | Same flags; only `SGLANG_ENABLE_ELASTIC_MEM_POOL` differs (0 vs 1); both use the Python tree core; run one after the other on the same card | Both servers start with full = SWA = 52,505 tokens. The workloads are `bench_serving` random with `--random-range-ratio 0.5`. They follow the gpt-oss sequence in `scripts/emem/dev.sh`, with fewer prompts. | Run | Prompts | In / out | Concurrency | Throughput (tok/s) off → on | Duration | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 128 | 8192 / 1024 | 128 | 1077 → 1268 (**+17.7%**) | -15.1% | -13.0% | +17.7% | | 2 | 256 | 2048 / 1024 | 256 | 1296 → 1594 (**+22.9%**) | -18.6% | -22.2% | +20.1% | | 3 | 128 | 8192 / 1024 | 128 | 1046 → 1300 (**+24.4%**) | -19.6% | -20.6% | +23.4% | - **All requests succeeded.** There were no leak-check failures, scheduler exceptions or device faults. - **More work per batch:** mean running requests went from 10.2 to 15.1, and mean generation throughput from 222 to 276 tok/s (server logs). TPOT rises because each decode step carries more requests, while total throughput and TTFT improve. - **One resize** at t = 236 s moved 288 cu_pages from the SWA pool to the full pool. The full pool grew from 52,505 to 77,823 tokens and SWA shrank to 28,671. The resize took 227 ms (tail eviction 0.2 ms, SWA shrink 71 ms, full grow 156 ms). ![token usage, running requests and throughput] ![pool capacity and resize breakdown] ### Static splits vs elastic This follows the layout of #13581: two static splits, plus elastic memory started from the worse of the two. Each config runs on its own B60, with the gpt-oss workload from `scripts/emem/dev.sh`: 512 prompts, 8192 in / 1024 out, `--random-range-ratio 0.5`, concurrency 128. | Config | Full / SWA tokens at start | Duration | Total throughput (tok/s) | Mean TTFT | Mean running requests | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | static, `--swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.6` | 65,632 / 39,379 | 2879 s | 1227 | 586 s | 8.4 | | static, `--swa-full-tokens-ratio 1.0` | 52,505 / 52,505 | 3263 s | 1082 | 672 s | 6.6 | | **elastic**, `--swa-full-tokens-ratio 1.0` | 52,505 / 52,505 | **2675 s** | **1320** | **543 s** | **10.0** | - **Elastic beats both static splits.** Starting from the 1.0 split, it has 22% more throughput than the same split left static (18% shorter run), and 8% more than the better static split (0.6). It keeps moving memory to the full pool beyond what a fixed ratio gives. - **Two resizes:** the full pool went 52,505 → 75,775 → 86,015 tokens, and SWA went 52,505 → 30,719 → 20,479. The resizes took 240 ms and 113 ms. In the elastic row of the chart, SWA usage steps up at each resize as its pool shrinks. Running requests rise from about 7 to 10, then to 12-14. - **No failures:** all 512 requests succeeded in every config, with no leak-check failures or scheduler exceptions. ![static splits vs elastic] ### TP=2 Two B60s, `--tp 2`, same flags otherwise. Each pool starts at 379,045 tokens. - **512 × 16384/1024, concurrency 256:** all requests succeeded at 2,567 tok/s total. - **Two resizes:** | Time | Full | SWA | |---|---|---| | 20:51 | 565,247 | 196,607 | | 21:25 | 655,359 | 106,495 | Both ranks logged the same sizes within a second of each other. Each resize took 370-574 ms. They moved 182,438 and 90,112 tokens, against 25,318 for the first one-card resize. - **Same speed as static TP=2 at 8192 input:** elastic ran at 2,999 tok/s and static at 3,059 tok/s (128 × 8192/1024). Elastic memory did not resize there. - **Fixed prompts:** TP=2 changes one of the five prompts between runs. Static TP=2 does the same with no resizes, so this is not caused by elastic memory. - **Workaround:** these runs set `TORCHINDUCTOR_USE_STATIC_CUDA_LAUNCHER=0`. With torch 2.14.0+xpu, Inductor's static Triton launcher segfaults on the first TP=2 request, with or without elastic memory. ### Soak One elastic server ran for 2 hours. It alternated 128 × 8192/1024 (concurrency 128) and 256 × 1024/1024 (concurrency 256) for 8 rounds, 3,072 requests in all. - **No failures:** every request succeeded, with no leak-check failures, scheduler exceptions or device faults. - **Two resizes, both early:** the pools resized twice in the first 6 minutes and ended at full 86,015 / SWA 20,479 tokens. 467 of 469 planned shrinks were cancelled. - **Flat device memory:** `xpu-smi` showed 18.13-18.16 GiB for the server from the second resize to the end. - **Same output:** the fixed prompts after the soak matched the ones from before any resize. ## Unit tests `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_elastic_allocator.py` has 8 CPU tests (`base-a-test-cpu`): - **Bookkeeping:** the shrink, borrow and cancel cases check that no slot is lost or handed out twice. - **Regression cases:** the device sync before unmap, both shrink floors, the skipped tree walk, returning leftover pages, and the signal handling. These cases fail on the code before the fixes. The kvcached-backed pools need kvcached and a GPU, so CI doesn't exercise them. ## Limitations - **Scope:** hybrid-SWA models with both full-attention and SWA layers, at `--page-size 1`, MHA/GQA with the NHD layout. MLA, PD disaggregation, HiCache and speculative decoding are not supported. Models that are not hybrid-SWA log a warning and run normally. - **Tree core:** requires the Python `UnifiedTreeCore`. - **intel_xpu with gpt-oss:** sgl-kernel-xpu builds whose non-paged kernels reject attention sinks fail on gpt-oss with `intel_xpu --page-size 1`. The results above use `triton`. - **Resize rate:** in the A/B run above, 113 of 114 planned SWA shrinks were cancelled while waiting for the tail to drain, because the usage gap fell back under the trigger. The trigger ratio and thresholds are tunable; they were left at their defaults here. - **Short requests don't trigger it:** with #13581's 1024/1024 workload (1,024 prompts, concurrency 128) on one card, elastic memory never resized: - **Mixed lengths:** the full pool peaked at 83%, below the 90% map threshold. - **Equal lengths:** the full pool reached 100%, but all 27 planned SWA shrinks were cancelled. Requests finish together, so the SWA tail drains only when the full pool empties too. - **One direction only:** every resize in these runs grew the full pool. In the soak, SWA usage reached 99% after its pool shrank, but it never ran 20 points above full usage, so no pages moved back to SWA. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #41596548536](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41596548536) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #41596548534](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41596548534) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #41596548316](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41596548316) > [!TIP] > Base CI only covers the core cases, and its workload may not exercise your change. +        start_time = time.perf_counter()
+        self._evict_tail()
+        if len(self.candidate_unmap_pages) != self.size - self.candidate_size:

+            logger.warning(

+                f"({len(self.candidate_unmap_pages)=}, {self.size=}, "
+                f"{self.candidate_size=})"
+            )
+            return 0

+        # forward may still read freed or just-evicted tail slots.
+        torch.get_device_module(self.device).synchronize()

+        kept = self.candidate_unmap_pages[self.candidate_unmap_pages <= cur_size]

+        self.size = cur_size
+        self.candidate_size = cur_size

+
+        logger.info(
+            f"elasticmem: {self.pool_name} reduce to {cur_size} took "
+            f"{(time.perf_counter() - start_time) * 1000:.2f} ms"
+        )
+        return unmap_num

+        start_time = time.perf_counter()
+        assert not self._shrink_pending()
+

+            expand_size = min(expand_size, self.max_size - self.size)

+            return 0

+

+        return self._empty_pages()

+        return self.candidate_size < self.size

+            f"elasticmem: {self.pool_name} evict_tail took "
+            f"{(time.perf_counter() - start_time) * 1000:.2f} ms"
+        )

+        size_swa: int,

+            kvcache,
+            need_sort,
+            req_to_token_pool=req_to_token_pool,
+        )
+        assert not self._swa_req_ring, "elasticmem does not support the SWA req ring"

+            dtype,
+            device,
+            kvcache.full_kv_pool,
+            need_sort,
+            max_size=max_size_full,
+        )
+        self.swa_attn_allocator = ElasticTokenToKVPoolAllocator(
+            size_swa,
+            dtype,
+            device,
+            kvcache.swa_kv_pool,
+            need_sort,

+        )

After a failed scan, an equal-length cache node can become unlocked while another becomes locked, leaving both `tail_in_use.numel()` and `evictable_size` unchanged even though the tail is now drainable. This branch then skips the index lookup on subsequent scheduler passes until a count changes, so a pending cold-pool shrink can remain stuck despite the newly evictable tail. Invalidate this cache when index membership changes rather than keying only on counts.

detail.body: [Feat] mem_cache: Elastic hybrid-SWA KV pools (kvcached VMM), with an Intel XPU path ## Motivation This PR ports sgl-project/sglang#13581 onto current main and adds an Intel XPU backend. With `SGLANG_ENABLE_ELASTIC_MEM_POOL=1`, the full-attention and sliding-window (SWA) KV pools of a hybrid-SWA model no longer have fixed sizes. Each pool reserves a large virtual range and backs only its current size with physical pages. The two pools trade pages at runtime: when one pool runs hot and the other runs cold, the cold pool's tail is drained and unmapped, and the freed memory is mapped into the hot pool. Total device memory stays the same; only the split between the pools changes. On gpt-oss-20b on an Intel Arc Pro B60, elastic memory raised throughput by 18-24% and cut mean TTFT by 13-22% across three workloads, using the same device memory. ## Dependencies - **[sgl-project/sglang#13581](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/13581)** (open), "Integration with elasticmem": the design this PR builds on. The first commit re-implements it on current main. If #13581 merges first, this PR rebases onto it and keeps only the XPU commit and the fixes listed under "Changes from #13581". - **[ovg-project/kvcached#501](https://github.com/ovg-project/kvcached/pull/501)** (open), "Intel XPU (Level Zero) backend for kvcached VMM": required for the XPU path. `ElasticXPUMHATokenToKVPool` calls `kvcached.vmm_ops`, which needs kvcached built from that PR with `KVCACHED_BACKEND=xpu`. The CUDA path keeps #13581's `kvcached.etensor` requirement and does not depend on #501. ## Modifications | Commit | Scope | |---|---| | Port elasticmem (kvcached VMM) hybrid-SWA pools onto main | The orchestrator, allocators and CUDA pool; configurator and scheduler wiring; startup validation; post-capture KV sizing turned off under elastic memory; CPU unit tests | | elasticmem: add an XPU path backed by kvcached Level Zero | `ElasticXPUMHATokenToKVPool`, its XPU startup checks, the XPU docs and `scripts/emem/dev_xpu.sh` | ### How it works - **`ElasticMempoolOrchestrator`** (`mem_cache/elastic/elasticmem_orchestrator.py`) picks the hottest and coldest pool by token usage. It resizes when all three hold: - the usage gap is at least `SGLANG_ELASTIC_MEM_RESIZE_TRIGGER_DIFF_RATIO` (0.2); - the hot pool is above `SGLANG_ELASTIC_MEM_MAP_THRESHOLD` (0.9); - the cold pool is below `SGLANG_ELASTIC_MEM_UNMAP_THRESHOLD` (0.8). - **`ElasticTokenToKVPoolAllocator`** (`mem_cache/elastic/elastic_allocator.py`) marks the cold pool's tail as a shrink candidate and withholds its free slots. - The shrink happens once every in-use tail slot can be evicted from the radix tree. Until then it waits, or it is cancelled if the pools even out. - The withheld slots still count as available, so admission is unchanged. - **`ElasticSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator`** owns the orchestrator and both sub-allocators. After each resize it re-syncs the `SWAKVPool` sizes and the full-to-SWA index mapping. - **Pools:** `ElasticMHATokenToKVPool` on CUDA (kvcached `ETensor`), and `ElasticXPUMHATokenToKVPool` on XPU (kvcached `vmm_ops`, see below). - **Scheduler:** `maybe_init_elastic_mem` attaches the allocator to the tree cache, and `try_resize` runs after each scheduled batch. - **`UnifiedTreeCore.component_evictable_device_indices`** reports which slots can be evicted, so a tail is shrunk only when it can be drained. ### Changes from #13581 - **Device sync before unmap:** unmap is not ordered with the stream. With overlap scheduling, the forward still in flight can read slots that were just freed or evicted. The allocator therefore synchronizes the device before it unmaps. The cost is one wait per shrink. - **Shrink floors:** each pool stops shrinking at a floor that keeps a max-length request schedulable. This keeps the scheduler's startup capacities and request-length limits valid: - the full pool keeps at least `max_req_len`; - the SWA pool keeps at least the sliding window plus one prefill chunk, or `max_req_len` when chunked prefill is off; - neither floor goes above the pool's startup size. - **Leftover pages:** pages too few for the hot pool to use go back to the cold pool instead of staying unmapped. - **Cheaper drain checks:** while a shrink is pending, the full-tree walk behind `component_evictable_device_indices` runs again only after the number of in-use tail slots or the evictable total changes. - **Shutdown handling:** kvcached shuts down at exit, and before a terminating signal whose handler is still the default. Signals that are ignored or have a Python handler are left alone, so an ignored signal no longer shuts kvcached down while the process keeps running. - **Tree core default:** main defaults `SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND` to rust, and only the Python core has `component_evictable_device_indices`. When the variable is unset, elastic memory picks python, as `--enable-kv-cache-sharding` does. An explicit non-python choice is refused. - **Startup validation** refuses: - devices other than CUDA and XPU; - `--page-size > 1`, unified memory, the page-major layout, the memory saver and speculative decoding; - PD disaggregation and `--enable-hierarchical-cache` (both register KV buffers by row count once, and a resize changes the row count); - mxfp8/fp4 KV, `SGLANG_USE_HND_KVCACHE`, and pure-SWA models. - **Env vars** are renamed to `SGLANG_ENABLE_ELASTIC_MEM_POOL` and `SGLANG_ELASTIC_MEM_*`. ### XPU pool - **kvcached backend:** uses `kvcached.vmm_ops` with kvcached's Level Zero backend (ovg-project/kvcached#501): - `init_kvcached` runs once per process; - `create_kv_tensors` creates one allocator group per pool; - `map_to_kv_tensors` / `unmap_from_kv_tensors` work by page offset. One offset covers that page of K and of V in every layer. - **No zero page:** Level Zero has no shared zero page, so every row the pool exposes is mapped before first use. After each resize, the K/V views and `_kv_buffer_descs` are re-sliced to exactly `size + page_size` rows. The data pointers stay the same. - **Virtual range:** sized from total device memory. Physical memory only moves between the two pools. - **Page size 1:** `intel_xpu` serves `--page-size 1` through sgl-kernel-xpu's gather fallback (sgl-kernel-xpu#454), which is slower than its paged kernel. `--attention-backend triton` works where that build is missing, or where its non-paged path rejects attention sinks (gpt-oss). - **XPU startup checks:** kvcached must be installed, and kvcached's own SGLang autopatch (`ENABLE_KVCACHED` / `KVCACHED_AUTOPATCH`) must be off. ## Accuracy Tests gsm8k (`sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`, all 1,319 questions) on two servers side by side, each on its own B60 with the flags below. Each server ran gsm8k, then 128 × 8192/1024 requests, then gsm8k again. The elastic server resized once during the middle step (full 52,505 → 77,823 tokens, SWA 52,505 → 28,671). | Server | Before | After | Change | |---|---|---|---| | elastic | 0.544 | 0.542 | -0.2 | | static | 0.510 | 0.528 | +1.8 | The static server, which never resizes, moved 1.8 points between two runs, so the -0.2 is within run-to-run noise. Five fixed prompts at temperature 0 (64 new tokens) gave identical text: - static vs elastic; - elastic before vs after its resize; - elastic before any resize vs after the 2-hour soak below. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Measured on the current head of this branch. In these runs the shrink floors don't bind: the full pool only grew, and the SWA floor (128 + 4096 tokens at the B60 default chunk size) is far below the 20,479-token minimum the SWA pool reached. The device sync before unmap is included in the resize times below. **Setup:** | | | |---|---| | Hardware | Intel Arc Pro B60 (24 GB), one card per server | | Driver | compute runtime 26.18.38308.1, Level Zero loader 1.26.2 | | Software | SGLang main `51d5502aff` + this PR, torch 2.14.0+xpu, kvcached with the XPU backend, sgl-kernel 0.11.0 | | Model | openai/gpt-oss-20b | | Flags | `--device xpu --attention-backend triton --page-size 1 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 1.0 --context-length 65536` | | A/B | Same flags; only `SGLANG_ENABLE_ELASTIC_MEM_POOL` differs (0 vs 1); both use the Python tree core; run one after the other on the same card | Both servers start with full = SWA = 52,505 tokens. The workloads are `bench_serving` random with `--random-range-ratio 0.5`. They follow the gpt-oss sequence in `scripts/emem/dev.sh`, with fewer prompts. | Run | Prompts | In / out | Concurrency | Throughput (tok/s) off → on | Duration | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 128 | 8192 / 1024 | 128 | 1077 → 1268 (**+17.7%**) | -15.1% | -13.0% | +17.7% | | 2 | 256 | 2048 / 1024 | 256 | 1296 → 1594 (**+22.9%**) | -18.6% | -22.2% | +20.1% | | 3 | 128 | 8192 / 1024 | 128 | 1046 → 1300 (**+24.4%**) | -19.6% | -20.6% | +23.4% | - **All requests succeeded.** There were no leak-check failures, scheduler exceptions or device faults. - **More work per batch:** mean running requests went from 10.2 to 15.1, and mean generation throughput from 222 to 276 tok/s (server logs). TPOT rises because each decode step carries more requests, while total throughput and TTFT improve. - **One resize** at t = 236 s moved 288 cu_pages from the SWA pool to the full pool. The full pool grew from 52,505 to 77,823 tokens and SWA shrank to 28,671. The resize took 227 ms (tail eviction 0.2 ms, SWA shrink 71 ms, full grow 156 ms). ![token usage, running requests and throughput] ![pool capacity and resize breakdown] ### Static splits vs elastic This follows the layout of #13581: two static splits, plus elastic memory started from the worse of the two. Each config runs on its own B60, with the gpt-oss workload from `scripts/emem/dev.sh`: 512 prompts, 8192 in / 1024 out, `--random-range-ratio 0.5`, concurrency 128. | Config | Full / SWA tokens at start | Duration | Total throughput (tok/s) | Mean TTFT | Mean running requests | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | static, `--swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.6` | 65,632 / 39,379 | 2879 s | 1227 | 586 s | 8.4 | | static, `--swa-full-tokens-ratio 1.0` | 52,505 / 52,505 | 3263 s | 1082 | 672 s | 6.6 | | **elastic**, `--swa-full-tokens-ratio 1.0` | 52,505 / 52,505 | **2675 s** | **1320** | **543 s** | **10.0** | - **Elastic beats both static splits.** Starting from the 1.0 split, it has 22% more throughput than the same split left static (18% shorter run), and 8% more than the better static split (0.6). It keeps moving memory to the full pool beyond what a fixed ratio gives. - **Two resizes:** the full pool went 52,505 → 75,775 → 86,015 tokens, and SWA went 52,505 → 30,719 → 20,479. The resizes took 240 ms and 113 ms. In the elastic row of the chart, SWA usage steps up at each resize as its pool shrinks. Running requests rise from about 7 to 10, then to 12-14. - **No failures:** all 512 requests succeeded in every config, with no leak-check failures or scheduler exceptions. ![static splits vs elastic] ### TP=2 Two B60s, `--tp 2`, same flags otherwise. Each pool starts at 379,045 tokens. - **512 × 16384/1024, concurrency 256:** all requests succeeded at 2,567 tok/s total. - **Two resizes:** | Time | Full | SWA | |---|---|---| | 20:51 | 565,247 | 196,607 | | 21:25 | 655,359 | 106,495 | Both ranks logged the same sizes within a second of each other. Each resize took 370-574 ms. They moved 182,438 and 90,112 tokens, against 25,318 for the first one-card resize. - **Same speed as static TP=2 at 8192 input:** elastic ran at 2,999 tok/s and static at 3,059 tok/s (128 × 8192/1024). Elastic memory did not resize there. - **Fixed prompts:** TP=2 changes one of the five prompts between runs. Static TP=2 does the same with no resizes, so this is not caused by elastic memory. - **Workaround:** these runs set `TORCHINDUCTOR_USE_STATIC_CUDA_LAUNCHER=0`. With torch 2.14.0+xpu, Inductor's static Triton launcher segfaults on the first TP=2 request, with or without elastic memory. ### Soak One elastic server ran for 2 hours. It alternated 128 × 8192/1024 (concurrency 128) and 256 × 1024/1024 (concurrency 256) for 8 rounds, 3,072 requests in all. - **No failures:** every request succeeded, with no leak-check failures, scheduler exceptions or device faults. - **Two resizes, both early:** the pools resized twice in the first 6 minutes and ended at full 86,015 / SWA 20,479 tokens. 467 of 469 planned shrinks were cancelled. - **Flat device memory:** `xpu-smi` showed 18.13-18.16 GiB for the server from the second resize to the end. - **Same output:** the fixed prompts after the soak matched the ones from before any resize. ## Unit tests `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_elastic_allocator.py` has 8 CPU tests (`base-a-test-cpu`): - **Bookkeeping:** the shrink, borrow and cancel cases check that no slot is lost or handed out twice. - **Regression cases:** the device sync before unmap, both shrink floors, the skipped tree walk, returning leftover pages, and the signal handling. MLA, PD disaggregation, HiCache and speculative decoding are not supported. Models that are not hybrid-SWA log a warning and run normally. - **Tree core:** requires the Python `UnifiedTreeCore`. - **intel_xpu with gpt-oss:** sgl-kernel-xpu builds whose non-paged kernels reject attention sinks fail on gpt-oss with `intel_xpu --page-size 1`. +class ElasticTokenToKVPoolAllocator(TokenToKVPoolAllocator, ElasticAllocator):
+    """page_size=1 allocator over an `ElasticMHATokenToKVPool` that can shrink
+    its tail or grow at the end.

+    ones sit in `candidate_unmap_pages` (still counted as available), and the
+    shrink happens once every in-use tail slot is evictable from the tree.
+    A shrink never goes below `min_size` slots.

+        dtype: torch.dtype,
+        device: str,

+

+    def can_be_candidate(self) -> bool:
+        return True
+

+        num_used = self.size - (self.available_size() + self._evictable_size_fn())
+        return num_used / self.size
+

+        return self.token_usage() < self.unmap_threshold

+        if self.max_size is not None and self.size >= self.max_size:
+            return False
+        return self.token_usage() > self.map_threshold
+
+    def mark_unmap_candidate(
+        self, is_candidate: bool
+    ) -> Optional[ElasticTokenToKVPoolAllocator]:
+        if not is_candidate:
+            self._cancel_shrink()
+            return None
+
+        assert not self._shrink_pending(), (
+            f"{self.pool_name}: {self.candidate_size=}, {self.size=}"
+        )
+        new_size = max(int((self.token_usage() + 1) / 2 * self.size), self.min_size)

+            return None

+            f"elasticmem: mark {self.pool_name} unmap candidate, "
+            f"{self.size=}, {self.candidate_size=}"
+        )

+        tail_in_use = self._tail_in_use_indices()

+            return True
+        evictable_size = self._evictable_size_fn()
+        if tail_in_use.numel() > evictable_size:
+            return False

+        # tail or the evictable total changes since the last failed check.
+        drain_key = (tail_in_use.numel(), evictable_size)

+                f"({len(self.candidate_unmap_pages)=}, {self.size=}, "

+        kept = self.candidate_unmap_pages[self.candidate_unmap_pages <= cur_size]
+        self.candidate_unmap_pages = self._empty_pages()
+        self.in_use = self.in_use[: cur_size + 1]
+        self.size = cur_size
+        self.candidate_size = cur_size
+        super().free(kept)
+
+        logger.info(
+            f"elasticmem: {self.pool_name} reduce to {cur_size} took "
+            f"{(time.perf_counter() - start_time) * 1000:.2f} ms"
+        )
+        return unmap_num
+
+    def expand(self, expand_size: int) -> int:
+        start_time = time.perf_counter()
+        assert not self._shrink_pending()
+
+        if self.max_size is not None:
+            expand_size = min(expand_size, self.max_size - self.size)

+            return 0

+        new_pages = torch.arange(
+            self.size + 1, cur_size + 1, dtype=torch.int64, device=self.device
+        )

+            (
+                self.in_use,
+                torch.zeros(
+                    (cur_size - self.size,), dtype=torch.bool, device=self.device

+            )
+        )

+        self.candidate_size = cur_size
+        super().free(new_pages)
+

+            f"elasticmem: {self.pool_name} expand to {cur_size} took "
+            f"{(time.perf_counter() - start_time) * 1000:.2f} ms"
+        )

+
+    def cu_page_to_token(self, cu_page_num: int) -> int:
+        return self._kvcache.cu_page_to_token(cu_page_num)
+
+    def update_size(self) -> None:
+        assert self.size == self._kvcache.size
+
+    # ---- helpers ----
+
+    def _empty_pages(self) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return torch.empty((0,), dtype=torch.int64, device=self.device)
+
+    def _no_indices(self) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self._empty_pages()
+
+    def _shrink_pending(self) -> bool:
+        return self.candidate_size < self.size
+
+    def _take_tail(self, boundary: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Remove and return the free slots above boundary."""
+        release_tail = self.release_pages > boundary
+        free_tail = self.free_pages > boundary
+        tail = torch.cat((self.release_pages[release_tail], self.free_pages[free_tail]))
+        self.release_pages = self.release_pages[~release_tail]
+        self.free_pages = self.free_pages[~free_tail]
+        return tail
+
+    def _return_candidate_pages(self, pages: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+        if self.need_sort:
+            self.release_pages = torch.cat((self.release_pages, pages))
+        else:
+            self.free_pages = torch.cat((self.free_pages, pages))

+    def _borrow_candidate_pages(self, need_size: int) -> None:
+        """Lend withheld tail slots to an alloc the free lists cannot cover.
+
+        The scheduler sized its eviction against available_size(), which
+        counts them; the borrowed slots just keep the shrink pending longer.
+        """
+        if not self._shrink_pending():
+            return
+        shortfall = need_size - (len(self.free_pages) + len(self.release_pages))
+        if shortfall <= 0:
+            return
+        self._return_candidate_pages(self.candidate_unmap_pages[:shortfall])
+        self.candidate_unmap_pages = self.candidate_unmap_pages[shortfall:]
+
+    def _cancel_shrink(self) -> None:
+        if not self._shrink_pending():
+            return
+        self._return_candidate_pages(self.candidate_unmap_pages)
+        self.candidate_unmap_pages = self._empty_pages()
+        self.candidate_size = self.size
+        self._failed_drain_key = None
+        logger.info(f"elasticmem: cancel {self.pool_name} shrink, {self.size=}")
+
+    def _tail_in_use_indices(self) -> torch.Tensor:
+        tail = self.in_use[self.candidate_size + 1 :]
+        return tail.nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0] + (self.candidate_size + 1)
+
+    def _evict_tail(self) -> None:
+        """LRU-evict from the tree until no in-use slot remains in the tail.
+
+        The tree cannot evict specific slots, so this may evict colder entries
+        below the tail too; can_do_unmap guarantees the tail itself is evictable.
+        """
+        start_time = time.perf_counter()
+        while True:
+            num_tail_in_use = int(self.in_use[self.candidate_size + 1 :].sum())
+            evictable = self._evictable_size_fn()
+            if num_tail_in_use == 0 or evictable == 0:
+                break
+            self._evict_fn(num_tail_in_use)
+            if self._evictable_size_fn() == evictable:
+                break
+        logger.debug(
+            f"elasticmem: {self.pool_name} evict_tail took "
+            f"{(time.perf_counter() - start_time) * 1000:.2f} ms"
+        )

+    """SWA allocator whose full and SWA sub-allocators trade physical pages

+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        size: int,
+        size_swa: int,
+        page_size: int,
+        dtype: torch.dtype,
+        device: str,

+        )

+            dtype,
+            device,

+        )

+            size_swa,
+            dtype,
+            device,
+            kvcache.swa_kv_pool,
+            need_sort,

+        # keeps last_loc == -1 mapping to -1 (see SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator).
+        self.full_to_swa_index_mapping = torch.cat(
+            [
+                torch.zeros(
+                    max_size_full + self.page_size, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
+                ),
+                torch.tensor([-1], dtype=torch.int64, device=device),
+            ]
+        )
+        self.clear()
+        self._kvcache.register_mapping(self.full_to_swa_index_mapping)

+        self.emem_orch = ElasticMempoolOrchestrator()
+        self.emem_orch.register_allocator(self)
+        self.emem_orch.register_allocator(self.full_attn_allocator)
+        self.emem_orch.register_allocator(self.swa_attn_allocator)
+
+    def _max_size_full(self) -> int:
+        full_layers = self._kvcache.full_kv_pool.layer_num
+        swa_layers = self._kvcache.swa_kv_pool.layer_num
+        total_layer_tokens = self._size_full * full_layers + self._size_swa * swa_layers
+        # 2x headroom over "every SWA page moved to full" (per-slot sizes can differ).
+        return 2 * max(
+            total_layer_tokens // max(full_layers, 1),
+            total_layer_tokens // max(swa_layers, 1),
+        )
+
+    def attach(
+        self,
+        *,
+        tree_cache: BasePrefixCache,
+        max_req_len: int,
+        sliding_window_size: int,
+        chunked_prefill_size: Optional[int],
+    ) -> None:
+        """Wire eviction and evictable lookups to the prefix cache, and set
+        how far each pool may shrink (never below its startup size).
+
+        The scheduler's startup capacities and request-length limits stay the
+        admission contract, so each floor keeps a max-length request
+        schedulable: the full pool holds the whole request, the SWA pool one
+        prefill chunk plus the window (the whole request without chunking).
+        """
+        self.full_attn_allocator.set_min_size(max_req_len)
+        swa_min_size = (
+            max_req_len
+            if chunked_prefill_size is None
+            else min(sliding_window_size + chunked_prefill_size, max_req_len)
+        )
+        self.swa_attn_allocator.set_min_size(swa_min_size)
+        if not isinstance(tree_cache, UnifiedRadixCache):
+            # Radix cache disabled: nothing is evictable, tails drain by frees.
+            return
+
+        self.full_attn_allocator.bind_tree_cache_fns(
+            evictable_size_fn=tree_cache.full_evictable_size,
+            evict_fn=lambda num_tokens: tree_cache.evict(
+                EvictParams(num_tokens=num_tokens)
+            ),
+            evictable_indices_fn=lambda: tree_cache.component_evictable_device_indices(
+                ComponentType.FULL
+            ),
+        )
+        self.swa_attn_allocator.bind_tree_cache_fns(
+            evictable_size_fn=tree_cache.swa_evictable_size,
+            evict_fn=lambda num_tokens: tree_cache.evict(
+                EvictParams(swa_num_tokens=num_tokens)
+            ),
+            evictable_indices_fn=lambda: self._full_to_swa_indices(
+                tree_cache.component_evictable_device_indices(ComponentType.SWA)
+            ),
+        )
+
+    def try_resize(self) -> None:
+        self.emem_orch.try_resize()
+
+    def resize(self, config) -> None:
+        raise NotImplementedError("elasticmem does not support post-capture resize")
+
+    def swa_capacity_and_available(self, *, full_capacity, swa_capacity):
+        # The scheduler's startup capacities go stale after a resize; report live ones.
+        return (
+            (self._size_full, self.full_available_size()),
+            (self._size_swa, self.swa_available_size()),
+        )
+
+    def _full_to_swa_indices(self, full_indices: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        swa_indices = self.full_to_swa_index_mapping[full_indices]
+        return swa_indices[swa_indices > 0]
+
+    # ---- ElasticAllocator: the composite only re-syncs sizes ----
+
+    def can_unmap(self) -> bool:
+        return False
+
+    def can_map(self) -> bool:
+        return False
+
+    def reduce(self) -> int:
+        raise NotImplementedError()
+
+    def expand(self, expand_size: int) -> int:
+        raise NotImplementedError()
+
+    def cu_page_to_token(self, cu_page_num: int) -> int:
+        raise NotImplementedError()
+
+    def token_usage(self) -> float:
+        raise NotImplementedError()
+
+    def update_size(self) -> None:
+        self._size_full = self.full_attn_allocator.size
+        self._size_swa = self.swa_attn_allocator.size
+        assert self._kvcache.full_kv_pool.size == self._size_full
+        assert self._kvcache.swa_kv_pool.size == self._size_swa
+        self._kvcache.size = self._size_full
+        self._kvcache.size_swa = self._size_swa
+        # Unbacked full slots must not map to a SWA slot.
+        self.full_to_swa_index_mapping[self._size_full + 1 : -1] = 0
+        logger.info(
+            f"elasticmem: sizes updated, full={self._size_full}, swa={self._size_swa}"
+        )

+        current_device_id = f"cuda:{torch.cuda.current_device()}"

+                self.esize,
+                self.page_size,
+                (self.head_num, head_dim),
+                self.store_dtype,
+                current_device_id,
+                free_memory,

+        for ek, ev in zip(self.ek_buffer, self.ev_buffer):

+        return total_map_num, self.size

+import os

+def parse_log_file(file_path):
+    """Parse log file and extract token usage, running requests, throughput, and timing data"""
+    full_token_usage = []
+    swa_token_usage = []
+    running_req = []
+    gen_throughput = []
+    timestamps = []
+
+    # Data for timing measurements
+    timing_timestamps = []
+    timing_values = []
+    timing_labels = []
+
+    with open(file_path, "r") as f:
+        start_time = None
+        for line in f:
+            # Extract timestamp from the beginning of the line
+            timestamp_match = re.match(r"\[([0-9-]+ [0-9:]+)\]", line)
+            actual_timestamp = None
+            if timestamp_match:
+                timestamp_str = timestamp_match.group(1)
+                actual_timestamp = datetime.strptime(timestamp_str, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
+                if start_time is None:
+                    start_time = actual_timestamp
+            else:
+                continue
+
+            # Look for prefill or decode batch lines
+            if "Prefill batch" in line or "Decode batch" in line:
+                # Extract full token usage and swa token usage
+                full_match = re.search(r"full token usage: ([0-9.]+)", line)
+                swa_match = re.search(r"swa token usage: ([0-9.]+)", line)
+                req_match = re.search(r"#running-req: ([0-9]+)", line)
+
+                # Extract generation throughput for decode batches
+                gen_throughput_match = re.search(
+                    r"gen throughput \(token/s\): ([0-9.]+)", line
+                )
+
+                if full_match and swa_match and req_match:
+                    full_token_usage.append(float(full_match.group(1)))
+                    swa_token_usage.append(float(swa_match.group(1)))
+                    running_req.append(int(req_match.group(1)))
+
+                    # Add generation throughput if available, otherwise 0
+                    gen_throughput.append(
+                        float(gen_throughput_match.group(1))
+                        if gen_throughput_match
+                        else 0.0
+                    )
+
+                    # Calculate time intervals in seconds from the first timestamp
+                    interval = (actual_timestamp - start_time).total_seconds()
+                    timestamps.append(interval)
+
+            # Extract timing information (took xxx ms)
+            took_match = re.search(r"took ([0-9.]+) ms", line)
+            if took_match:
+                timing_value = float(took_match.group(1))
+                timing_values.append(timing_value)
+
+                # Extract the operation name before "took"
+                operation_match = re.search(r"\] ([^,]*?) took", line)
+                if operation_match:
+                    operation = operation_match.group(1).strip()
+                else:
+                    operation = "operation"
+                timing_labels.append(operation)
+
+                # Store actual timestamp for timing data
+                if actual_timestamp:
+                    interval = (actual_timestamp - start_time).total_seconds()
+                    timing_timestamps.append(interval)
+
+    return (
+        timestamps,
+        full_token_usage,
+        swa_token_usage,
+        running_req,
+        gen_throughput,
+        timing_timestamps,
+        timing_values,
+        timing_labels,
+    )
+
+
+def plot_data(

+    timing_values,
+    timing_labels,

+    # With shared x-axis, only the bottom subplot needs x-label

After a failed scan, an equal-length cache node can become unlocked while another becomes locked, leaving both `tail_in_use.numel()` and `evictable_size` unchanged even though the tail is now drainable. This branch then skips the index lookup on subsequent scheduler passes until a count changes, so a pending cold-pool shrink can remain stuck despite the newly evictable tail.
